reference_behaviors: Resolve one global address for each of the exact ordered 45 ntdll symbols, then read the same address in each process.
Compare all 32 bytes; keep the first occurrence order of byte groups and processes.
One group gives empty distinct text and its process count. Two or more groups compare only the first two; ties choose group two as majority.
Total Implementations is the majority group size, not the total count across groups.
Unreadable function windows are skipped, not zero-filled. Native coverage metadata records successful and missing reads.
limitations: Real differential evidence is x64 Windows 10 build 15063 and Windows 7 build 7601 only. Intel x86 has shared decoder/paging coverage, not positive plugin acceptance. ARM64 is rejected.
Both default cases resolve functions through captured PE export tables; a nonempty exact user-module PDB source and further mixed WOW64 configurations require additional evidence.

The captured read path permits directly mapped valid/transition pages and excludes prototype/pagefile reconstruction for PE headers, exports and byte windows. Ordinary PESymbols still uses its existing recovery path.
PE PDB acquisition retains the existing CodeView resolver. This batch does not certify all differences between exact CodeView lookup and reference scanning of module memory.
Process/VAD and symbol discovery diagnostics remain partial. Matching output does not prove coverage of unreadable processes or establish a malware verdict.

Three-or-more-group behavior intentionally follows the fixed plugin and ignores later groups when computing its three output columns; native metadata reports how many functions have additional groups.
At most MAX_OBJECTS successful byte-window observations are retained; a limit reports partial while preserving earlier groups. Collection and output loops check cancellation.
Success and partial result caches are bypassed because external module PDB resources can change symbol addresses.
Full option/failure contracts, additional kernels and captured-page export corruption cases remain outstanding.
